summary: Computes a quaternion product using 3DNow! packed floating-point intrinsics. Reads the two packed float pairs of quaternions a2, a3 and a4, builds three cross-product-like terms (v7, v8, v9) from the component pairs of a3 and a4 via punpck/pfmul/pfsub, then assembles the two output halves of the product into a1[0] and a1[1] with pfmul/pfacc and sign-flip XOR against the packed negative-zero constant 0x8000000000000000 (backed by global qword_5AF980). MMX/3DNow state is cleared with _m_femms at entry and exit, and the output buffer pointer a1 is returned. The packet's ABI name QuaternionProduct3DNow is LEGACY-trusted.

operations.description: Clear MMX/3DNow state via _m_femms before the arithmetic sequence.
Load the second component pairs of the a3 and a4 inputs (v5 = a3[1], v6 = a4[1]).
Build cross-product term v7 from the component pairs of a3 and a4 using punpckhdq/punpckldq, pfmul and pfsub.
Build cross-product term v8 from the component pairs of a3 and a4 using punpckhdq/punpckldq, pfmul and pfsub.
Build cross-product term v9 from the component pairs of a3 and a4 using punpckldq/punpckhdq, pfmul and pfsub.
Load the a2 quaternion component pairs (v10 = a2[1], m64_u64 = a2[0]) used to assemble the product.
Assemble the first output half from v7/v8/v9 and a2 via pfmul, sign-flip XOR against 0x8000000000000000 (packed negative-zero constant backed by global qword_5AF980), and pfacc.
Build the sign-flip masks v12 and v15 from 0x8000000000000000 using psrlqi/psllqi, and derive v13/v14 via pxor against v12.
Assemble the second output half from v7/v8/v9/v13/v14/v15 and a2 via pfmul, pfacc and sign-flip XOR masks.
Store the first 64-bit half of the quaternion product into a1 at offset 0x0.
Store the second 64-bit half of the quaternion product into a1 at offset 0x8.
Clear MMX/3DNow state via _m_femms after the arithmetic sequence.
Return the output buffer pointer a1.

clean_pseudocode: a1[0] = quaternion_product_half(v7, v8, v9, a2[0], a2[1], sign_mask);
a1[1] = quaternion_product_half(v7, v8, v9, a2[0], a2[1], sign_mask);
